name: Pea
grown_as: A hardy annual vegetable sown in spring, grown up twigs or netting: shelling peas, mangetout (flat pods eaten whole) and sugar snap (round pods eaten whole). Most have white flowers; some mangetout have purple flowers. Some modern varieties are 'semi-leafless', with tendrils in place of leaflets. Drawn as an ordinary leafy white-flowered pea. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A climbing annual 45 cm to 1.5 m (dwarf to tall), hairless, the whole plant blue-green. Weak round stem climbing by branched tendrils at the ends of the leaves; the very large leafy stipules at each joint look like the main leaves.

leaf.type: Compound, pinnate: 1 to 3 pairs of leaflets, the central stalk ending in a branched tendril
leaf.leaflets: Leaflets in pairs, unstalked, symmetrical. At the base of each leaf a pair of huge leafy stipules, larger than the leaflets, clasping the stem.
leaf.outline: Leaflets oval, 2 to 6 cm. Stipules broad and half heart-shaped, wrapping round the stem.
leaf.base: Leaflets rounded; stipules with a rounded lobe below the joint
leaf.tip: Rounded or with a tiny point
leaf.margin: Leaflets entire or with a few faint teeth; stipules toothed along their lower edge
leaf.surface: Hairless with a grey waxy bloom; stipules often with whitish mottling
leaf.stalk: Short, ending in the branched tendril

flower.form: A pea flower: an upright back petal (the standard), two side petals (the wings) and two lower petals joined into a boat-shaped keel between the wings
flower.petals: Five: a large rounded upright standard, two wings and a small keel
flower.colour: White (in some mangetout, a pink-purple standard with deep purple wings)
flower.behind: A green calyx with five pointed teeth, the upper two broader
flower.carried: One to three on a stalk from the leaf joint, the flowers facing out

fruit: Pods hanging from the leaf joints: shelling peas 6 to 10 cm, plump, smooth, green, with 4 to 9 round peas; mangetout flat with the peas barely showing; sugar snap round and fleshy. Dry pods go pale buff and papery. Seed: a round pea 5 to 8 mm, smooth or wrinkled, green to cream when dry.
seedling: The seed leaves stay in the pea underground. A pale shoot comes up with small scale leaves, then leaves of one pair of leaflets with a simple tendril and the big stipules.
winter: Nothing: an annual, cleared after cropping

leaf: 1 to 3 pairs of oval leaflets ending in a branched tendril
a pair of big leafy stipules clasping the stem, bigger than the leaflets
bloom: a pea flower: large round standard, two wings, keel
seed: a round pea, smooth or wrinkled
seedling: a thin shoot with small paired leaflets and a first tendril
young: a weak stem climbing a support with tendrils
flower: white pea flowers in ones to threes from leaf joints on a climbing plant
crop: smooth green pods hanging from the leaf joints
seedhead: dry pale buff papery pods hanging from the joints

look_alikes: Sweet pea has a winged hairy stem, only one pair of leaflets and narrow stipules. Vetches have many pairs of narrow leaflets and small stipules. Broad bean has no tendrils.
